MA4344 overview

MA4344 Topic Guide

Group Actions

Translate symmetry into homomorphisms, orbits and stabilisers.

Purpose

Construct action homomorphisms and use orbit-stabiliser without losing track of the set being acted on.Exam use: Action law, point, stabiliser calculation, orbit index and partition/Burnside check are shown.

Question plan

  1. State G, X and the rule g·x.
  2. Check e·x=x and (gh)·x=g·(h·x).
  3. Find orbit Gx and stabiliser Gx.
  4. Use |Gx|=[G:Gx] for finite G; identify the kernel for faithfulness.
  5. Question interpretation: For an action, verify identity and compatibility; for orbit-stabiliser, name the point and compute its stabiliser; for counting, separate orbits from elements.

Key terms

Action, orbit, stabiliser, kernel, faithful action, permutation representation ρ:G→Sym(X), conjugation action.Rapid recall: An action is a homomorphism G->Sym(X); Orb(x) is in bijection with G/Stab(x), so |Orb(x)|=[G:Stab(x)] for finite G; Burnside averages fixed-point counts.

Proof method

Send g to the permutation x↦g·x. Check ρ(gh)=ρ(g)ρ(h); its kernel consists of elements fixing every point. If the action is faithful, ρ embeds G in Sym(X).Exam workflow: Write the action map, find stabilisers by solving g.x=x, use orbit-stabiliser, and audit that orbit sizes partition X.

Worked simple proof

Claim: S3 acting on {1,2,3} has |Orb(1)|=3. Every point can be sent to 1 by a permutation, so the orbit is the whole set; therefore |Stab(1)|=6/3=2.

Practice 1 — orbit-stabiliser for the square action [9 marks]

Prompt. Let D4 act on a square’s vertices. Find a vertex stabiliser and use orbit-stabiliser to calculate its orbit. Question-demand diagnosis. Identify actual symmetries before substituting cardinalities. Fastest route. List identity and the reflection through the selected vertex/opposite vertex, then use |G|=|Orb(v)||Stab(v)|. Topic-specific trap. D4 here has eight symmetries, not four.

Let D4 act on the four vertices of a square. For a vertex v, the stabiliser contains identity and the reflection through v and the opposite vertex, so has size 2. Since |D4|=8, orbit-stabiliser gives |Orb(v)|=8/2=4, as expected. For the action on diagonals, rotations by 0 and 180 fix both diagonals while 90 and 270 swap them; reflection counts depend on axis and can feed Burnside.

Graduated exam bridge

1. Let C4 rotate the vertices of a square. Find the orbit and stabiliser of one vertex. Check: orbit size 4; stabiliser is trivial.

2. Prove a faithful action of G on n points gives G≤Sn. Check: use the action homomorphism and trivial kernel.

Practice 2 — Burnside count of binary necklaces [8 marks]

Prompt. Count length-four binary necklaces up to rotation. Question-demand diagnosis. Burnside requires fixed-string counts for each rotation before averaging. Fastest route. Use fixed counts 16,2,4,2 for rotations by 0,1,2,3 positions. Topic-specific trap. Dividing 16 by four misses strings with nontrivial rotational symmetry.

Paper-style synthesis: use Burnside to count binary necklaces of length 4 under rotations. Check fixed strings for rotations 0,1,2,3 are 16,2,4,2, so orbits=(16+2+4+2)/4=6.

Mistakes

  • Using orbit-stabiliser before checking the action.
  • Calling an action faithful when a nonidentity element fixes all points.
  • Confusing a point stabiliser with the kernel.
  • Recovery rule: The stabiliser is a subgroup of G, while the orbit is a subset of X; do not multiply their sets or swap their sizes.

Checklist

  • I can state the action axioms.
  • I can form the permutation representation.
  • I can compute an orbit and stabiliser.
  • Final 60-second audit: Action law, point, stabiliser calculation, orbit index and partition/Burnside check are shown.
